text:
maria: Heads-up — seeing repeated OOMs on node inference-gpu-12 since ~03:47 UTC. Runtime containers keep restarting. Logs include CUDA errors and kv-cache warnings: "kv_paged: fragmentation growth, slow leak detected". Opening thread to coordinate live mitigation.
kevin: I’m on it. Linking INC-2026-112. Any customer-facing 503s yet?
sophie: Telemetry: hosted API error rate rose to 2.6% at 03:50 in us-west-2, 95th latency spiked ~600ms. A small subset of queries hit fallback; dedicated tenants saw degraded throughput on a few pods.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED INC-2026-112 — priority P1 (OOMs causing service errors). Runbook: paged-attn/kvcache leaks -> triage steps posted.
maria: Relevant log tail (from runtime container on inference-gpu-12):
```
[03:46:21] runtime: cuda error: cudaErrorIllegalAddress at 0x7f8b...
[03:46:22] kv_cache: page_alloc: failed to reserve contig slab (requested=64MB)
[03:46:22] kv_cache: fragmentation: resident_pages=1243 free_chunks=12 growth=+7 since last sweep
[03:46:23] runtime: container exiting (OOM)
```
kevin: Ok — likely slow fragmentation in paged allocator + hot KV growth triggers OOM under burst. Immediate plan (short list):
  1) Route-level mitigation: switch heavy routes to smaller model variants / short-context model to reduce KV pressure.
  2) Node containment: cordon + drain problematic node to avoid repeated restarts.
  3) Runtime mitigation: increase kv eviction aggressiveness and force a cache compaction on affected pods.
  4) If needed, restart runtime with `--kv-compact-on-start` flag and temporarily lower batch sizes.
sophie: For (1) I can flip routing to fallback-small in us-west-2 for high-throughput routes now — minimal quality hit. Propose 10 min canary then full switch.
kevin: Do it. Command I’m running: 
```
# cordon node
kubectl cordon inference-gpu-12
# drain evict non-daemonset pods (graceful)
kubectl drain inference-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=60
```
kevin: Also applying an emergency kv policy change via ops API to increase eviction ratio to 0.85 for runtime pool:
```
curl -X POST https://ops.internal/api/runtime/kv-policy -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' -d 'evict_ratio=0.85&compact=true'
```
deploy-bot: rollout request accepted — applying config to runtime-pool-us-west-2 (3/3 pods).
maria: After the evict/compact change, I see resident_pages drop ~20% on the affected pods. Error rate in us-west-2 trending down: 2.6% -> 1.1% in 7 minutes.
sophie: Routing switch: canary to 5% at 03:56, scaling to 100% at 04:02. No customer complaints yet; alerting shows success.
kevin: Restarted runtime on node after draining, node remains cordoned. Post-restart logs show no immediate cuda illegal address traces. Keeping node out of rotation until we validate compaction stability for 30m.
sre-shift: Note for postmortem: capture sequence lengths distribution, batch size changes, and kv page-size fragmentation metrics. Possible follow-ups: add periodic compaction job and adjust allocator heuristics to trigger earlier.
maria: Customer impact summary for ops: ~2.6% error spike for hosted API in us-west-2 for ~15min window, no long-term data loss, Dedicated tenants had brief throughput degradation but fallbacks held. No SLA breach so far but close on tail latency.
kevin: Current status: mitigation applied, node cordoned + drained, kv policy tightened, routing fallback applied and then rolled back after stability. Monitoring will keep watch for 30m; will escalate to infra team if fragmentation resumes.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT INC-2026-112 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Assigned: kevin (oncall).
sophie: leaving watchstanding for next 30m, will ping if any regression. :thumbsup: 
maria: Thanks team — documenting next steps in INC-2026-112 ticket for postmortem and allocator follow-ups.
